The equations of a model, as Markdown

Source: R/methods_md.R
methods_md.Rd

Writes the model in mathematical notation for a methods section. The Data section names the response, the dimensions and the predictors. The Model section holds the likelihood, the linear predictors and the latent dynamics in one display equation, with a glossary of every symbol. The Priors section states every prior the Stan program applies. The Implementation section gives the call that fits the model and the software versions the fit recorded. The equations are LaTeX inside $$ fences, which Quarto, R Markdown and MathJax render.

Usage

methods_md(object, file = NULL, implementation = TRUE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mvgam'
methods_md(object, file = NULL, implementation = TRUE, heading_level = 2L, ...)

Arguments

object

A fitted mvgam or jsdgam object, or a prefit from mvgam(..., run_model = FALSE).

file

Optional path. The Markdown is written there and returned invisibly.

implementation

Logical. TRUE (the default) adds the Implementation section.

...

Unused. Anything passed here is refused.

heading_level

Integer Markdown level of the section headings. The default 2 writes ## Model. A higher level nests the sections under a heading of the host document.

Value

A character string of class mvgam_methods_md, which prints as its Markdown.

See also

how_to_cite() writes the matching methods paragraph and its references. prior_summary() lists the priors as a table.

Other posterior summaries: VarCorr.mvgam(), bibtex(), how_to_cite.mvgam(), hypothesis.mvgam(), index-mvgam, mcmc_plot.mvgam(), mvgam_draws, pairs.mvgam(), posterior_interval.mvgam(), ranef.mvgam(), smooths.mvgam(), summary.mvgam()

Author

Nicholas J Clark

Examples

# \dontrun{
set.seed(13)
simdat <- sim_mvgam(family = poisson(), n_series = 1L,
                     n_timepoints = 120L, trend_model = AR())
mod <- mvgam(y ~ s(x, k = 5), trend_formula = ~ AR(p = 1),
              data    = simdat$data_train,
              family  = poisson(),
              chains  = 2, silent = 2)
#> Warning: 5 of 2000 (0.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.

# The equations, glossary and priors as Markdown
md <- methods_md(mod)
md
#> ## Data
#> 
#> $y$: non-negative integer counts
#> 
#> $N = 90$ observations, $S = 1$ series, $T = 90$ time points
#> 
#> Predictors:
#> 
#> - $x$: continuous covariate
#> 
#> ## Model
#> 
#> $$
#> \begin{aligned}
#> t &\in \{1, \ldots, 90\} \\
#> y_{i,t} &\sim \text{Poisson}(\mu_{i,t}) \\
#> \log \mu_{i,t} &= \alpha + f_{x}(x_{i,t}) + \eta_{i,t} \\
#> f_{x}(x) &= \sum_{m=1}^{K_{x}} \beta^{(x)}_m B_m(x) \\
#> \eta_{i,t} &= \phi_{1} \eta_{i,t-1} + \epsilon^{(\eta)}_{i,t} \\
#> \epsilon^{(\eta)}_{i,t} &\sim \text{Normal}(0, \sigma_\eta)
#> \end{aligned}
#> $$
#> 
#> where:
#> 
#> - $i$ indexes series, $t$ indexes time
#> - $\mu_{i,t}$: conditional mean of $y_{i,t}$
#> - $\alpha$: population intercept
#> - $f_{x}$: thin plate regression spline in $x$, basis size $K_{x} = 5$, smoothing SD $\sigma^{(s)}_{x}$
#> - $\eta_{i,t}$: latent state at series $i$ time $t$
#> - $\epsilon^{(\eta)}_{i,t}$: process innovation, SD $\sigma_\eta$
#> - $\phi_{l}$: autoregressive coefficient at lag $l$
#> 
#> ## Priors
#> 
#> $$
#> \begin{aligned}
#> \alpha &\sim \text{StudentT}(3, 1.6, 2.5) \\
#> \sigma^{(s)}_{x} &\sim \text{StudentT}(3, 0, 2.5) \\
#> \sigma_\eta &\sim \text{Exponential}(2) \\
#> \phi_{1} &\sim \text{Normal}(0, 0.5)
#> \end{aligned}
#> $$
#> 
#> Every other parameter takes an improper flat prior on its support.
#> 
#> ## Implementation
#> 
#> Fitted with mvgam 2.0.0 (brms 2.23.2; Stan 2.40.0 via cmdstanr). Hamiltonian Monte Carlo: 2 chains, 1000 warmup + 1000 sampling iterations per chain.
#> 
#> ```
#> mvgam(
#>   formula       = y ~ s(x, k = 5),
#>   trend_formula = ~AR(p = 1),
#>   data          = simdat$data_train,
#>   family        = poisson(),
#>   backend       = "cmdstanr",
#>   chains        = 2,
#>   iter          = 2000,
#>   warmup        = 1000
#> )
#> ```

# Written to a file, nested under a level-two heading
methods_md(mod, file = tempfile(fileext = ".md"), heading_level = 3L)

# Next, forecast(mod) predicts the times after the training data
# }
